correctness.rationale: For each circle Fourier mode, direct integration gives a rational numerator affine in n^2 in each parity; nonnegativity of the full sequence is equivalent to four slope/endpoint inequalities. The denominators are strictly positive for a>0, and all n>=2 modes remain strictly positive even on the boundary, implying strict positive definiteness via a Vandermonde argument. Uniform small-offset expansion and global confinement to O(1/omega) of an integer prove sharp high-frequency half-width gamma(a). Deterministic quadrature/finite-index diagnostics agreed; analytic arguments, not samples, prove the claims.

value.rationale: Oscillatory covariance on a circle poses a real validity problem: noninteger frequency is not a circle character and can break positive definiteness even when the unmodulated envelope is valid. A sharp four-number decision rule across infinitely many Fourier modes, strict interpolation on all admissible boundaries, and infinitely many disjoint high-frequency windows of exact asymptotic width are structurally informative beyond a routine parameter substitution. The explicit bound is useful for covariance-design frequency choices and diagnosing spectral aliasing at the antipodal cusp.
